title: Day 37 · Week 5, Day 2 — Physiology: the sickness that isn't in the morning — the hormone from the baby that causes it, what actually works, and the three-question score that tells you when to call
summary: Your baby is 2.5–4.5 mm at the turn to Carnegie stage 11: the rostral neuropore closing, the heart tube bending and starting to pump, the otic pit formed. The Physiology this week is hers. The daily-diary studies: 80% of 363 women had symptoms, mean onset Day 39 and cessation Day 84 with the peak in week 9, 53% of vomiting between 6 a.m. and noon, and 35% of employed women losing a mean 62 hours of work (Gadsby 1993); nausea confined to the morning in 1.8% and lasting all day in 80%, half still symptomatic at 14 weeks, at chemotherapy-grade intensity (Lacroix 2000); 69.4% of 93,753 women worldwide, 14% severe, hyperemesis 1.1% (Einarson 2013); 1.5% of 8.2 million English pregnancies admitted, prior HG the strongest predictor (Fiaschi 2016); quality of life measurably lower (Lacasse 2008). The cause: GDF15, a hormone made overwhelmingly by the feto-placental unit and acting on her brainstem, with severity set by how much of it she was used to before pregnancy — β-thalassaemia women with chronically high GDF15 barely get sick (Fejzo 2024, Nature). The smell question (Cameron 2014: no sharper nose, just more intolerable smells). What works, by tier: Cochrane 2015 (41 trials, 5,449 women — no high-quality evidence for any single intervention, which is not the same as ineffective); ginger for nausea, not vomiting (12 RCTs, 1,278 women); doxylamine–pyridoxine, first-line in ACOG PB 189 and RCOG GTG 69, cleared by 27 studies (RR 0.95) and modestly effective (PUQE −4.8 vs −3.9); metoclopramide (28,486 exposed, no signal) and ondansetron (88,467 exposed; clefts 11.1 → 14.0 per 10,000, RR 1.24; no cardiac signal) as second-line; ketonuria is not a severity marker; thiamine on admission. The PUQE-24 score with its thresholds, the same-day call list, the Day 41 preview on 'sickness is a good sign', and why the management — food, smell and mornings — is the father's.
action: Tonight, build the nausea kit. A box by her side of the bed with plain crackers and a bottle of water, refilled every night until she says stop. Put the three PUQE questions and the scoring in your phone notes under the practice's after-hours number from Day 28. Say out loud that the kitchen and the mornings are yours until twelve weeks — shopping, cooking cold and plain with the windows open, clearing up, and whatever has to happen between six and noon. And one question for her to put to the practice or a pharmacist this week, before it's bad: if the sickness gets going, should she start vitamin B6, at what dose, and should doxylamine be added? Get the plan now, so it exists on the day she needs it.
